title: The abstract reports the spillovers the 2016 corrigendum withdraws
published: Working within the analytic framework proposed by Bowers et al. (2013), [[I find evidence of spillovers]], and present estimates of direct and indirect treatment effects. [[The total causal effect of the experimental intervention appears to be twice as large as reported originally.]]
corrected: NA
note: The corrigendum withdraws both claims: “There is insufficient statistical evidence to conclude that indirect exposure to information altered legislator behavior.” On the corrected analysis the total causal effect is 9 votes (entry 13) against the 5.6 the difference in means implies, about one and a half times as large, and the part of it beyond the direct effect rests on indirect effects whose confidence regions include zero. The abstract is reproduced as published.

title: Figure 1's upper confidence bound is one grid step too high
published: The 95% confidence region extends from −0.34 to [[0.02]].
corrected: The 95% confidence region extends from −0.34 to [[0.01]].
note: The deposited code reports as each region's upper bound the first hypothesis outside it rather than the last one inside it, so every upper bound it reports sits one step of the grid too high; the step is 0.01 here and 0.025 in every other figure. The lower bounds are correct. Zero lies inside the region on either reading, as the $p$-value of slightly more than 0.05 at zero says. Entries 15 and 17 to 22 correct the same rule in the appendix.

title: Figure 2's point estimates are those of the faulty similarity matrix
published: The highest p-value point is ([[−0.300, −0.225]]), constituting the point estimates of direct and indirect effects.
corrected: The highest p-value point is ([[−0.250, −0.150]]), constituting the point estimates of direct and indirect effects.
note: The corrigendum, doi 10.1017/XPS.2016.8, traces the published estimates to a coding error: the ideological similarity matrix set every off-diagonal entry to one, as if all legislators were equally close to one another in ideological space. It reports the corrected pair as −0.250 for the direct effect and −0.150 for the indirect effect. The maintained code rebuilds the matrix from Equation (1) and returns the same pair. Figure 2 is regenerated from the corrected analysis.

title: Figure 2's confidence regions cross zero once the similarity matrix is corrected
published: [[The 95% confidence region does not cross zero for either the direct or indirect effect, indicating that these results are statistically significant. These results provide evidence that legislators whose close colleagues received treatment were less likely to vote for the bill.]]
corrected: NA
note: On the corrected surface the direct effect's region runs from −0.625 to the top of the grid searched, 0.2, and the indirect effect's from −0.350 to 0.150, so both cross zero. The corrigendum withdraws the inference the second sentence draws: “There is insufficient statistical evidence to conclude that indirect exposure to information altered legislator behavior.” It prints the corrected regions as [−0.625, 0.175] and [−0.325, 0.200]. The upper bounds differ by the rule entry 3 describes, which the note on the corrigendum corrects in its own entry 1, and the indirect lower bound by one grid step because the maintained code draws assignments with R's current sampler; under the sampler of 2016 it returns the corrigendum's bound. The passage is reproduced as published.
